issues.legal_issue: A residence order cannot permit occupation of a property that was never a shared household of the parties in a domestic relationship.
material_facts: The respondent sought to occupy a property belonging to the appellant under an interim order.
The respondent admitted that she had never lived with the appellant in that property.
The respondent had not been excluded from or dispossessed of that property after living there.
issues.conclusion: The interim order permitting occupation of the property could not be sustained and was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(f) and 2(s) of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 define a domestic relationship and a shared household by reference to living together in the relevant household in such a relationship. Sections 17 and 19 provide a right of residence and authorize residence orders, but those provisions did not support an order granting occupation of a property the parties had never shared in a domestic relationship. The court did not rely on an earlier case for this issue.

predicates.challenge_to_interim_residence_order: A proceeding challenges an interim order permitting a person to occupy a property as a residence.
predicates.parties_never_lived_in_target_household: The person seeking residence and the other party never lived together in the property in a domestic relationship.
predicates.aggrieved_person_not_excluded_from_targe: The person seeking residence had not lived in the property and was not later excluded or dispossessed from it.

issues.definition: When an interim residence order is challenged and the parties never shared the target household and the person seeking residence was not excluded from it, the order is set aside.

issues.legal_issue: An appeal should not be withdrawn from the ordinary appellate court to the High Court without a reasoned basis when doing so removes an additional forum for review.
material_facts: The respondent's appeal from the dismissal of her application under the domestic violence legislation was pending before an Additional Sessions Judge.
The High Court treated the respondent's petition as one seeking transfer and withdrew the appeal to itself.
The Supreme Court found no reason justifying withdrawal and concluded that the transfer deprived the appellant of an additional forum for scrutiny.
issues.conclusion: The order withdrawing the appeal to the High Court was set aside, and the appeal was to be heard by an Additional Sessions Judge nominated by the High Court's Chief Justice.
issues.legal_principle: The court held that, absent a reason justifying the transfer, withdrawing an appeal from the appellate authority deprived a party of a valuable additional forum for review. The appeal arose under Section 29 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005; the High Court treated the petition as one under Section 407 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Section 327 of the Code and Article 227 of the Constitution were mentioned as possible further remedies. The appellant relied on A.R. Antulay v. Ram Naik, (1988) 2 SCC 602, in support of the asserted legal position; the court's stated basis for its decision was the lack of reason for withdrawal and the loss of an additional forum.

predicates.challenge_to_withdrawal_of_appeal: A proceeding challenges an order transferring a pending appeal from its ordinary appellate court to a higher court.
predicates.transfer_without_case_specific_reason: The transfer was ordered without a case-specific reason that justified removing the appeal from its ordinary appellate court.
predicates.transfer_eliminates_additional_appellate: The transfer deprives a party of an additional forum for review of the appellate decision.

issues.definition: When a challenged transfer lacks a case-specific reason and eliminates an additional forum for appellate review, the withdrawal is set aside and the appeal is returned to the ordinary appellate court.
